GIG — Built for the stage

An interface designed for the stress of a gig

Most backing track apps are designed for the studio. GwavaTRACKS is designed to be used under pressure at the gig.

Cheap Mac and no internet

macOS 12 Monterey and above — 2015 Macs. All the data is on the Mac hard disk, so no requirement for internet. The Backup/Restore feature means you can quickly set up a backup Mac.

Simple error-proof operation

High contrast on near-black. Large song titles, big nav buttons, customised keys, colour-coded rows. Perfect for the high stress of a live gig.

Panic stop, Auto-follow, Finale

Hit the spacebar to kill the song and reset. Turn on Auto Follow for any song and the next one plays automatically. Assign a Finale song and trigger it with a single keypress to cue that song.

Live waveform, BPM, and track progress

Real-time waveform display with elapsed and remaining time always visible. Current song and "up next" displayed prominently so the whole band knows where you are.

Remote apps

The Mac app can also be controlled by an iPad, iPhone or Android. Connected securely by your Wi-Fi.

Quick setup with import from iTunes or CSV

Got your songs in iTunes / Music app or a spreadsheet? Your library is built in seconds. No re-entering everything by hand.

Video on the LED backwall or screen

Drive a video backdrop on a second screen. You can have a default band video or override it for different songs.

Song editor — audio, video, lighting theme per song
Data sync — bring a backup Mac to every gig

Full Backup and Restore. Sync everything to a second machine before the show. If anything goes wrong on the night, switch and keep playing.

Settings — backup, restore, keyboard mappings

From zero to encore

Quick to set up, fast to change

1

Import setlist from CSV

Artist, title, BPM. It creates a setlist and adds new songs to the song library. Or import songs from CSV. Build a setlist manually — add songs and drag into order.

2

Add backing tracks

Drag the audio files onto the songs — MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, AIFF. If you want, drag videos onto the band or each song — MP4, M4V, MOV.

3

Run rehearsals and soundcheck

Quicklists is a separate setlist of colour-coded songs at the bottom of the performance view. Use it for test and soundcheck songs, or songs not in the setlist — like Happy Birthday.

4

Play the gig

Hit Enter. At the end of every song, the next is cued — just hit Enter to keep the show flowing. Panic Stop kills the track and resets. Hit Finale to jump straight to the end of the show.

Setlist manager — colour-coded lighting themes, auto follow, finale

PRO — Lighting designer and controller

A full lightshow.
Zero crew required.

A choreographed lightshow has always been out of reach unless you're at a large venue with a budget for a lighting designer spending days programming, and a lighting engineer at every gig to run it.

GwavaTRACKS PRO changes all of that. The lighting designer builds a complete set of scenes for each song in seconds using AI or presets. Trigger each lighting scene or chase — a sequence of scenes — from a MIDI file attached to each song. The light show runs automatically when you launch the song, all night.

Add your fixture and rig configuration

Set up each fixture type you own and then drag and drop the channel definitions. Create a Lighting Project with your rig setup — fixtures and their DMX addresses.

Design scenes and chases in seconds

Choose colours, styles and patterns and the lighting designer will create a chase with scenes. Use AI (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini) and it costs less than 10c to create 16 scenes.

Design using presets

Set colours and use the presets — sweep, figure 8, in/out odd/even — to quickly create chases and scenes for your LEDs and moving heads. See the show inside the designer.

Connect the chases and scenes to songs

Merge the chase and scenes into a lighting project and assign a MIDI note so the song MIDI file can trigger the chase or any scene. Use the simulator or connect the lights to audition the show.

Break the MIDI limit

There are only 127 MIDI notes available. But we've created themes where you can use 127 notes per theme for any song. Don't like the look? Just flip the theme at the song level.

AI lighting designer — describe the vibe, get scenes instantly
🔌

One piece of hardware. That's it.

GwavaTRACKS drives industry-standard DMX512 via the Enttec Pro USB controller. Plug it into the Mac, one DMX cable to the rig, and you're live. Works with any DMX512 fixture or rig.
